When your app is distributed as an APK (especially one built using the PWA/Netlify/PWABuilder method we discussed), updating it is actually much easier than a standard app store process. 

There are two types of updates: **Content Updates** and **App Shell Updates**.

### 1. Content Updates (Automatic & Instant)
Since your APK is essentially a high-performance "wrapper" around your hosted website (Netlify/Vercel/etc.), **you do not need to build a new APK for code changes.**

*   **How it works:** When you update your code and deploy it to your hosting provider (like dragging the folder to Netlify Drop again), the changes go live on the URL.
*   **The User Experience:** The next time a user opens the app on their phone, it will automatically fetch the new files from the web. If they are offline, the "Service Worker" (built-in PWA tech) will show the old version until they reconnect, at which point it will silently update in the background.

### 2. App Shell Updates (Requires New APK)
You only need to generate and distribute a **new APK file** if you change the "native" parts of the app. You must do this if you change:
